result.title: When Imperfect Automated Fact-Checking Backfires: Social Learning in the Presence of Misinformation
result.summary: Automated fact-checking tools, cheap and fast but imperfect, are increasingly available on social platforms. We study when such tools can backfire in a sequential social learning model of misinformation. Agents observe an article's reliability and their predecessors' actions, which indicate whether they liked or disliked the article. They may also pay to fact-check it. We examine how welfare, defined as the probability of a correct cascade, changes when a free, error-prone automated tool supplements costly but perfectly accurate manual fact-checking. Two opposing effects arise. Broader use of fact-checking helps agents escape wrong cascades. At the same time, errors from the automated tool can mislead agents who would otherwise have verified the article perfectly, reducing the likelihood of correct cascades. We prove that adding the tool strictly lowers welfare for articles of intermediate reliability when truthful articles are not too informative and manual checking is sufficiently costly. Simulations show that the tool can help on either side of the intermediate range, and that it improves on manual-only checking on average only above a threshold accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 用序贯社会学习模型刻画：平台提供免费但会出错的自动事实核查、同时保留付费但完全准确的人工核查时，智能体何时放弃精确核查、福利（正确级联概率）如何变化；证明在文章可靠性居中且人工核查成本足够高时，加入该工具反而严格降低福利。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心机制是「廉价但有噪的验证信号使本会精确核验的智能体提前停止并被误导」，这与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选和 LOOK/STOP 的收益—成本权衡可能同构，可作为验证成本与停止决策建模的概念参照，具体对应关系可供核查。
